subject: microbiology
title: History, bacterial morphology and physiology: core exam essentials

steps.tx: Microbiology began with **Leeuwenhoek**, who first saw bacteria using a simple microscope in the seventeenth century. **Pasteur** later showed that microbes arise from other microbes, which supports the germ theory of disease. **Lister** applied antiseptic methods to surgery, reducing infection. Jenner's smallpox vaccination with cowpox is a classic early milestone. Know who did what, since exams often pair a name with a single discovery.

steps.tx: The bacterial **cell wall** is made of **peptidoglycan**, a rigid mesh containing muramic acid. Gram-positive walls are thick, with **teichoic acids** and no outer membrane. Gram-negative walls are thin, with an outer membrane carrying **lipopolysaccharide**, also called endotoxin. Endotoxin is heat stable and forms part of the cell wall. Exotoxins are proteins, heat labile and highly antigenic, and can be converted into toxoids.

vis.alt: Cross-sectional comparison of bacterial envelopes: Gram-positive bacteria have thick multilayered peptidoglycan with teichoic and lipoteichoic acids above a single cell membrane; Gram-negative bacteria feature an outer membrane with lipopolysaccharide endotoxin and porins, thin periplasmic peptidoglycan, and inner cytoplasmic membrane.
vis.caption: Bacterial envelope: Gram-positive has thick peptidoglycan and teichoic acid; Gram-negative has outer membrane LPS endotoxin and periplasm.

steps.tx: **Gram staining** uses four steps: crystal violet, iodine as a mordant, a decolouriser such as ethanol or acetone, and a counterstain. Gram-positive cells keep the violet colour and appear purple. Gram-negative cells lose it and take up the counterstain, appearing pink. **Ziehl-Neelsen** staining is an acid-fast method that uses carbol fuchsin, which binds the mycolic acid rich walls of mycobacteria. Methylene blue is not part of the Gram procedure.

steps.tx: The field contrasts purple cocci in clusters that retain **crystal violet iodine** against pink rods that lost it and took up **safranin counterstain**. The inset explains why: thick **peptidoglycan** traps the dye complex in Gram positive walls, while thin walls with an outer **lipopolysaccharide** membrane lose it. Colour plus shape therefore reports wall structure at a glance.
steps.say: This image teaches Gram stain reading. Purple clustered cocci kept the crystal violet iodine complex, marking thick walled Gram positive cells. Pink rods lost the violet during decolourising and took the pink counterstain, marking thin walled cells with an outer membrane. The wall inset shows the structural reason, so colour plus shape lets you infer wall type directly from the slide.

steps.tx: Surface **appendages** have distinct roles. **Flagella** give motility and may be monotrichous, lophotrichous or peritrichous. **Fimbriae** or pili are fine hair-like structures that act as organs of **adhesion**, and sex pili transfer DNA during conjugation. The **capsule** protects against phagocytosis and is usually lost on repeated subculture, reducing virulence. Capsules are best shown by India ink negative staining. Dipicolinic acid is a marker of **spores**. Light microscopy resolves about 300 nm, and dark ground microscopy makes slender spirochetes visible.
